title: Part 6
html:
Rishabha-parvata, Ramnad, Rameshvaram. The silent ascetic of Madhavi-vana. The Tamraparni and Kanyakumari. Travancore and King Rudrapati. Shringeri, the source of the Kaveri, Chandapur: the debate with Ishvara Bharati (pp. 101–122)

[p. 101]

1098The brahmana said, "You are Krishna; you have fulfilled me,"
and saying this he clasped both his feet tightly.

1099On leaving, the Lord told the brahmana [to stay],
but the brahmana left everything and ran after the Lord.

1100Sending the brahmana back, the son of Shachi
then went on to the Rishabha mountain.

1101On the Rishabha mountain lives Paramananda Puri;
the Lord hastened to see him.

1102He spoke much of Krishna with Puri,
and then came to the town of Ramnath.

1103In the town of Ramnath are Rama's footprints;
seeing them, the Lord shed tears.

1104His body filled with thrills and began to tremble,
and the Lord fell senseless to the ground.

1105Touching the lotus feet, my merciful one
shudders again and again, breathing hard.

1106Having seen the lotus feet, the son of Shachi
went on to see other holy places.

1107Going to the tirtha of Rameshvara and bathing there,
my Gaura-Hari had darshan of Shiva.

1108The Shiva named Rameshvara is of wondrous form;
seeing Shiva, Mahaprabhu bowed to him.

[p. 102]

1109Many sadhus always live there,
and then all the sadhus came one by one.

1110Seeing the Lord, a learned renunciant
became very eager to debate.

1111The Lord said, "I do not wish to debate;
I admit I have been defeated by you in argument."

1112Seeing his wondrous humility with his own eyes,
the sannyasi was dumbfounded and pondered inwardly.

1113The Lord said, "What are you thinking, sannyasi thakura?
Put away all this idle speculation.1

1114Putting idle speculation aside, with devotion
sing the glories of Krishna, brother, with a pure heart.

1115Worship Krishna, speak of Krishna, take Krishna's name;
taking Krishna's name, go to the eternal abode.

1116There is no way but Krishna — this is my counsel;
coming and going again and again, you will suffer.

1117What is the use of pride, good man?
What need is there to become a pandit in debate?

1118A sinful pandit builds his house in hell —
so everyone says, so the shastras have written.

1119One who knows many shastras yet lives by his whims —
what will that fool achieve by debating?

[p. 103]

1120One who cheats for the sake of money —
that unbeliever does not understand the words of scripture.

1121For one whose mind is busy with women and gold,
the study of the Vedas is a mockery.

1122One in whose heart envy is always at play
is punished by the lord of the ancestors2 with his own hand.

1123One whose heart melts at the Name of Hari —
he, in my view, is the great pandit.

1124One from whose eyes streams of bliss flow
when he chants the Name of Hari — he is called truly learned.

1125One who, however much he reads and hears, has no taste for Krishna —
he, brother, is a fool and always impure."

1126Hearing these words from the Lord's lips,
the yogi stayed silent for some time.

1127All the detached sannyasis, surrounding the Lord,
listened to his words, lost to themselves.

1128At last Gora-chand raised both his arms
and, drunk with the Name of Hari, toppled over.

1129Lord Chaitanya fell crashing down,
and the blow of a stone cut his chin.

1130Blood began to flow in streams,
and the excellent pandit carefully wiped it away.

[p. 104]

1131After three days of kirtana at Setubandha,
he went to the left to see Madhavi-vana.

1132In Madhavi-vana lives an ascetic under a vow of silence;
my beggar3 went to see him.

1133That sannyasi has a wondrous radiant form,
his white beard covering his chest.

1134His long nails have curled over;
he sits in silence, naked.

1135No cloth, no staff, no water-pot beside him.
Chaitanya Gosai gazed at him steadily.

1136He is utterly serene, his eyes closed;
the tree is his house, the sky his clothing.

1137He has no desires and is absorbed in austerity;
my Lord stood before him with folded hands.

1138Chaitanya spoke many humble words and praises,
yet the excellent sannyasi did not even look round.

1139Every three days all the renunciants
bring him alms of fruits and roots.

1140Every three days that great yogi
takes food and so sustains his life.

1141Breaking his meditation, the excellent yogi looked round,
and at that moment the Lord began to speak.

[p. 105]

1142The yogi understood nothing of the Lord's words,
and then he conversed with him in Sanskrit.

1143The worthy yogi listened calmly to his words
and spoke a few words with the Lord.

1144Having spoken a few words, the great yogi
cried "Chambani shiori!"4 and laughed.

1145Crying "Chambani shiori!", with a wholly pure heart
he bowed with a smile at the Lord's feet.

1146My Gora Raya bowed in return
and, floating in joy, sang the glories of Krishna.

1147Seeing the excellent yogi bow down,
all the sannyasis then clasped the Lord's feet.

1148Having spent time there in spiritual conversation,5 Gora Raya
left that place after seven days.

1149There is a tirtha called Tattvakundi6 there;
the Lord went there to bathe.

1150Then the river Tamraparni came into view,
and the Lord went there to bathe.

1151On the full-moon day of Magha, on the bank of the Tamraparni,
many pilgrims come to bathe.

1152Waiting there a fortnight,
on the full moon of Magha we went and bathed.

[p. 106]

1153Crossing the Tamraparni, the Lord
went along the seashore to see Kanyakumari.

1154There are no hills, forests or villages there;
only the sound of the sea can be heard.

1155Huge waves, rolling in there,
seem to be singing the praises of God consciously.

1156Seeing that, the heart is gladdened;
with the rising of feeling, his body thrilled.

1157The sand, heaped up like mountains,
seems to proclaim the glories of God.

1158The sea roars unceasingly, "hoo, hoo";
what more can I say — everything there is beautiful.

1159There is nothing to see, yet it is lovely;
there beauty is seen by one whose mind is pure.

1160Calling me, "Govinda!",
the Lord, with a slight smile, told me to bathe.

1161Waves like mountains come rushing in;
there he bathed with devotion.

1162After bathing, my Lord weeps, crying "Hari";
the love of his heart seemed to overflow.

1163His hair stood on end, his brow broke into sweat,
and his emaciated body was filled with thrills.

[p. 107]

1164After bathing, Gora Raya pondered
and, calling me, said, "Which way will you go?"

1165I said, "Whichever way the Lord goes,
that way the servant will go, to serve him."

1166After bathing, a large band of sannyasis
turned back towards Mount Sitala.

1167Nimai joined them and went along,
and I followed behind like a shadow.

1168After going fifteen kroshas we reached Sitala,
and there the band of sannyasis halted.

1169Chaitanya Gosai went beneath a tree,
and I could not think what alms to beg or where.

1170Understanding my mind, with a slight smile
the Lord said, "What are you worrying about?

1171We shall pass the night drinking the nectar of the Name,
and in the morning we shall get up and go wherever we like."

1172Saying this, Gora-chand closed his eyes
and sat motionless, leaning against the tree.

1173All the sannyasi thakuras, playing their khanjanis,7
began to sing, very sweet to hear.

1174Just then a merchant came there
and, giving alms to all, went away.

[p. 108]

1175Whole fruits and roots, milk and sugar —
he gave them as alms to everyone with devotion.

1176Receiving the alms, my heart was thrilled,
and the Lord took the milk and sugar and offered them.

1177All the sannyasi thakuras rose in the morning
and set off for the land of Trivinku,8 crossing the mountains.

1178The king of the land of Trivinku is very virtuous;
he cares for his subjects as for his own sons.

1179All the townspeople are skilled in hospitality;
they make a great commotion over guests.

1180Everyone tugs at the guests, vying for them,
and serves the guests with great affection.

1181The king here — his name is Rudrapati —
is father and mother to the poor, refuge of the helpless.

1182In this king's realm the subjects are very happy,
and all their hearts are full of love for the king.

1183How many elephants and horses are tied at the king's gate!
There is no shortage of food in his storehouses.

1184In three places in the town there are food-kitchens;
guests and travellers come and stay at them.

1185Each stays there as long as he likes;
all praise him, saying, "Blessed, blessed is the king!"

[p. 109]

1186In the evening we came to the town of Trivinku,
and the Lord sat beneath a tree with a joyful heart.

1187A villager brought parched grain,
and the Lord passed the night beneath the tree.

1188Next day the news spread,
and gradually the townspeople gathered.

1189Seeing Gora's wondrous state, everyone
came and stood there with folded hands.

1190Gora chants the Name of Hari with closed eyes,
and all, standing, praise him with pure hearts.

1191The Lord sits there, not a limb moving,
tears flowing from the corners of his eyes.

1192His hair on end, thrilled at heart;
seeing his state, the village people offer so many praises.

1193Some say, "Come to my house, sannyasi";
others say, "I love to look at you."

1194Some bring and offer fruits and roots,
but my Lord does not open his eyes to look.

1195Some say, "This sannyasi is no man.
Why else should such devotion arise on seeing him?

1196Seeing him, I want to give up worldly things;
my mind no longer wishes to live a household life."

[p. 110]

1197Some say, "Today the night passed happily;
seeing the sannyasi, my heart has been purified."

1198An old man came and said with devotion,
"Where is the sannyasi? Show him to me."

1199Seeing his eagerness, my Gora Raya
quickly got up and went over to him.

1200The old man bowed before the Lord
and brought him fruits, roots and parched grain.

1201Everyone whispered about this,
and hundreds of learned men came wishing to see him.

1202A brahmavadin came up
and raised the doctrine of advaita, and Chaitanya smiled.

1203Citing the Vedas, Vedanta and the proofs of scripture,
he explained it to him, and hearing it the man lost himself.

1204The Lord said, "Listen, listen, worthy sage:
the perfection of all practice is the love of Radha.

1205Radhika's subtle love is like a mountain;
without devotion no one can find the way to it.

1206Giving up her own happiness, beautiful Radhika,
mad for Krishna, renounced everything.

1207One who understands Sri Radha's deep love
does not die again and again.

[p. 111]

1208For one who is always floating on the doctrine of maya,
the truth of devotion does not dawn.

1209The choicest essence of love is mahabhava,
and Sri Radha is surely full of mahabhava.

1210Whoever understands this truth, worthy elder,
is not born and does not die again and again."

1211Then the Lord's glory spread through the land,
and gradually all sorts of people began to gather.

1212The king of this country, with great eagerness,
sent men to fetch the Lord.

1213The Lord said, "I have no business there;
I do not go to worldly men."

1214The royal messenger said, "Listen, sannyasi thakura,
why not go? You will get plenty of wealth.

1215Clothes, ornaments and whatever you want —
there you will get such riches without effort."

1216Understanding from the messenger's words what his intention was,
the Lord began to reason with him.

1217With a slight smile the Lord said:
"Listen, royal messenger, I have no need of wealth.

1218Into the company of those who are worms of worldliness
I never go. What use are riches to me?

[p. 112]

1219Worms of worldliness crave wealth;
wealth is the root of evil — this is my conviction.

1220Those who are drunk with wealth and forget the truth
always remain in the hell of worldliness.

1221The rich man does not know that the body is transient,
and regards wealth as the purpose of life."

1222Hearing this, the messenger grew angry
and went off to the king's gate to get his revenge.

1223Hearing the report from the messenger's mouth, King Rudrapati
was not at all angry with the sannyasi.

1224Hearing it word for word from the messenger,
he himself wished to see the sannyasi.

1225King Rudrapati set off to see the sannyasi;
full of devotion, he came out in haste.

1226Leaving his elephants and horses far behind,
he came to the sannyasi in very humble dress.

1227With two or four ministers, the worthy king
came near the Lord and said with devotion —

1228with folded hands Rudrapati said again and again:
"Be merciful and forgive my offence.

1229Without understanding, I summoned you;
forgive me that offence this time.

[p. 113]

1230Give me teaching in knowledge, saviour of the fallen:
why do living beings suffer grief and sorrow?"

1231The king is very learned in many shastras;
everyone says he is a great scholar of the Bhagavata.

1232Two or four learned gosais
came with him to receive instruction.

1233The Lord said, "King, you are most fortunate.
You know the Bhagavata — what more can I say?

1234You are well versed in many shastras, a great sage,
while I know nothing but Radha and Krishna."

1235As soon as he took Krishna's name, love welled up,
and tears began to stream down.

1236Drunk with love for Krishna, the Lord rose at once
and began to dance with arms outstretched.

1237Crying "Hari bol!", Gora lost consciousness
and, dancing, fell crashing to the ground.

1238Then the king rushed forward and lifted the Lord,
and at the same moment the maharaja grew drunk.

1239Crying "Hari!", the maharaja began to dance,
and his chest was flooded with tears.

1240His hair stood on end, he was filled with thrills;
falling in the dust, his body turned grey.

[p. 114]

1241Seeing the king's devotion, my Nimai
embraced the king and said, "Come, brother.

1242One whose eyes shed tears at the Name of Hari
is the apple of my eye.

1243Seeing your devotion, worthy king,
know for certain that my heart is soothed."

1244Saying this and sending the maharaja away,
the Lord went off to bathe.

1245The king sent many fruits and roots,
and the Lord, after his daily rites, made the offering.

1246Leaving people to serve the Lord,
the king went back to his capital with a happy heart.

1247Some bring fruits and roots, some bring flour,
some bring parched grain to the guest's lodging.

1248For Vishvambhara's sake people bustle about,
and now and then many people come and sit down.

1249Each brings and offers whatever he likes,
but Gora Raya says nothing, good or bad.

1250The land, ringed by mountains, is beautiful to see;
the spring waters flow most charmingly.

1251All around are huge neem trees;
their wondrous beauty is beyond words.

[p. 115]

1252There is a mountain there called Ramagiri;9
everyone extols its wondrous greatness.

1253All say that on its summit Ramachandra
stayed three days with Sita.

1254Having won the battle of Lanka, Rama, abode of virtues,
climbed this peak and rested.

1255Ramachandra with Sita and Thakura Lakshmana —
all three rested here.

1256Hearing this, the Lord was filled with longing
and climbed the mountain to see the place.

1257Where Rama and Sita had rested,
there my Gora went and bowed down.

1258Hundreds of people climbed with the Lord
to gaze with devotion at that Ramagiri.

1259This country is very extensive in breadth and length;
a fortnight passed while we crossed it.

1260Then he entered the town of Payoshni10
and was delighted to see Shiva-Narayana.

1261In the matha of Shringari11 live the disciples of Shankara;
going there, the Lord met with them.

1262All the disciples of Shankara, gathering together,
sat down to debate, examining the truth.

[pp. 116–117 — from the 1926 edition; these pages are missing in the base edition]

1263In the debate all the disciples admitted defeat,
and from the matha he went to see Matsya-tirtha.

1264Having visited Matsya-tirtha, the Lord came to Kachad,
and at Kachad had darshan of Bhagavati.

1265Here flows the river named Bhadra, daughter of the Krishna;12
having bathed, he went on to Naga-panchapadi.

1266All the people here are devotees of Rama;
here the Lord told me to beg alms.

1267I went round three houses begging,
and they all gave me plenty of flour.

1268Staying here three nights, my Lord
went on with everyone to Chitol,13 crossing the mountains.

1269Leaving Chitol, he went again to the bank of the Tungabhadra,
walking slowly, to bathe.

1270Having bathed on the bank of the river Tungabhadra,
my Gora, delighting all hearts, sings Krishna's glories.

1271The birthplace of the Kaveri is Kotigiri;14
he arrived there after wandering through many lands.

1272Having bathed at the source of the Kaveri,
the Lord Bhagavan went to the village of Chandapur.

1273On the left a mountain called Satya stands in splendour —
Satyagiri; I cannot describe its beauty.

1274From afar a blue line can be seen;
looking at its beauty soothes the eyes.

1275Seeing Satyagiri, the Lord bowed down
and, keeping Satyagiri on the left, went to the right.

1276Coming near the town of Chandapur,
he went and sat beneath a banyan tree.

1277In Chandapur lives a detached gosai;
hearing of him from people, Nimai went to meet him.

1278The gosai is indeed learned and knows many shastras;
a golden earring swings in one of his ears.

1279Gradually the gosai began quoting scripture
and started a conversation full of pride.

1280The sannyasi's name is Ishvara Bharati;
people say this gosai is an abode of all virtues.

1281Perceiving the sannyasi's pride in his heart,
the Lord smiled a little and turned his face away.

1282Lord Vishvambhara says nothing, good or bad,
and at last, irritated, the excellent sannyasi

1283says to the Lord, "You don't say a word;
I do not accept you as a learned pandit.

1284Everyone says you are very learned,
but I see in you not a trace of knowledge.

[p. 118]

1285You have made the whole country shout 'Hari bol',
but I see not the slightest merit in you.

1286I have heard you are learned in the shastras, yet you have nothing to say;
you wander about begging wherever you can.

1287You have neither learning nor knowledge to debate with.
Why then are the foolish so suddenly beguiled?

1288Who knows by what trick and stratagem
you show the subtle truth to everyone?

1289How you will get away after making the fools of this country shout 'Hari bol' —
I shall see through your cunning.

1290If you have the power, then debate;
this time I shall find out your wits and understanding."

1291Saying this, Bharati Gosai hurried off
and came back again and sat down with three companions.

1292The four of them sat on the four sides of the Lord,
and seeing this comedy the Lord began to laugh.

1293Bharati said, "You laugh it off;
but consider carefully what I say.

1294Tell me, which deity is to be worshipped?"
The Lord said, "What is there in the world but Krishna?"

1295Bharati said, "Hear the proof of scripture:
the one Brahman is the lord of all — so the Vedas teach.

[p. 119]

1296Wherever I look, I see everything as Brahman.
Tell me, how can this doctrine be refuted?"

1297The Lord said, "I don't know how to debate;
I admit that you are learned in every truth.

1298You are a great pandit in debate, gosai;
Nimai has been defeated by you.

1299If you like, I can write you a certificate of victory:
today I have admitted defeat in your debate."

1300Hearing this, the yogi grumbled and muttered,
and the Lord said, "Practise devotion — logic is far away.

1301Devotion brings Krishna — that is the conclusion.
Reduce the doctrines of the Vedas and Vedanta to dust.

1302Tell me, what is the fruit of discussing many shastras?
Without Krishna there is nowhere to stand."

1303Saying this, my Lord closed his eyes;
his hair stood on end and devotion overflowed.

1304Tears began to flow down his breast,
and the knot of his kaupina gradually came loose.

1305Trembling all over, his heart quaking, his body sweating,
he called out "Krishna!" and began to sway.

1306"O Krishna, where are you, merciful Lord?
Bestow devotion and purify my heart."

[p. 120]

1307Saying this, the Lord began to weep,
and the surge of his heart seemed to double.

1308Lord Vishvambhara hears nothing, good or bad,
and sobs and weeps unceasingly.

1309Seeing a tamala tree in front of him,
he ran, crying "Krishna!", and threw his arms around it.15

1310Seeing this state with his own eyes,
the yogi then clasped the Lord's feet.

1311The yogi said, "I beg you, let us not debate;
now my longing for Krishna is growing.

1312Seeing your state, young sannyasi,
I no longer have any wish to debate.

1313Give my heart the incomparable jewel of devotion;
this I humbly beg at your feet."

1314But the Lord does not hear these words of the yogi;
my Lord is soaking the earth with his tears.

1315In the surge of great ecstasy his body grew rigid,
and his body, the equal of gold, fell in the dust.

1316Crying "Krishna!", the Lord rolls on the ground,
his body grey with dust and pierced by thorns.

1317The yogi, sitting before him, began to weep,
and at once compassion for him arose in the Lord.

[p. 121]

1318Seeing Bharati's devotion, he put his hand on his back,
and with his hand on his back said a few words.

1319At the Lord's touch devotion arose in the yogi,
and his mind was immersed in the rasa of devotion to Krishna.

1320How great the Lord's mercy is cannot be told;
drunk with love, the yogi rolls in the dust.

1321The yogi said, "You are my Krishna.
When, Lord, will you come again and show yourself to me?"

1322The Lord said, "Do not say such words again.
Krishna is the lord of Vrindavana — that is the conclusion.

1323Without devotion the truth of Krishna does not dawn;
know for certain that Krishna is bound by the rope of devotion."

1324The yogi said, "I have seen through your trick.
Why do you throw dust in my eyes with your cunning?

1325Today I shall bind you with the rope of devotion;
today I shall snatch away both your sandals."

1326Saying this, Ishvara Bharati
seized the sandals and began to tug at them hard.

1327The Lord said, "Put your faith in Krishna;
from today your name is Krishnadasa."

1328Saying this, the Lord left Chandapur,
and the excellent yogi came with him a long way.

[p. 122]

1329Smiling, the Lord sent the yogi back,
and the excellent yogi bowed and went away.

1330Two days and nights we went on, crossing the mountains,
and in that time, search as we might, we found no village or town.

1331The path is very hard; I could not walk.
Only kadamba trees could be seen, row upon row.

1332Seeing the kadamba trees, Gora said to me,
"My Krishna plays beneath these trees."

1333Saying this, my Lord burst into distraught weeping
and walked on swaying, drunk with love for Krishna.

1334There I saw a tiger and was afraid.
[the second line of the couplet is missing in the edition]

1335I pointed out the tiger to the Lord with a sign,
but heard nothing from the Lord's lips, good or bad.

1336The tiger was drinking water at that place,
and I crept carefully along beside the Lord.

1337Gora went to the right, keeping the tiger on the left,
in ecstasy, his body drunk with the Name of Hari.

1338The tiger did not even look round at us,
but I kept looking back and walked quickly on.

1339Seeing how I behaved, with a slight smile
the Lord said, "What are you afraid of?"

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. Atal-patal, literally "abysses and nether worlds", i.e. empty, far-fetched speculation.
  2. The lord of the ancestors (Pitripati) is Yama.
  3. "My beggar" is an affectionate name for Chaitanya the sannyasi.
  4. An obscure exclamation (chambani shiori), apparently words in a local language, which Govinda records by ear.
  5. Ishta-goshthi: conversation about the beloved deity, spiritual discussion.
  6. The name is unclear in the edition (Tattvakundi).
  7. The khanjani is a small tambourine.
  8. Trivinku is Travancore (Tiruvitankur). The name of King Rudrapati also occurs in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9) as the king of Travancore.
  9. Compare "Ramagiri-ashramas" in Kalidasa's Meghaduta, to which the 1926 edition points in a footnote.
  10. Payoshni (Payasvini) is a river and district in Kerala; in CC Madhya 9 Chaitanya sees Shankara-Narayana there.
  11. Shringeri is the chief matha of the Shankara school.
  12. The river Bhadra, "daughter of the Krishna", is presumably the Tunga-Bhadra in the Krishna river system.
  13. Chitol is probably Chitradurga.
  14. Kotigiri is the source of the Kaveri (Talakaveri in the Coorg hills).
  15. The tamala is a dark-barked tree whose colour recalls Krishna.
